places.name: Uttar Pradesh
places.summary: India's most visited state for domestic travellers, home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Varanasi and the newly inscribed Sarnath.
places.seoTitle: Uttar Pradesh Travel Guide: Agra, Varanasi & Sarnath
places.seoDescription: Plan a trip to Uttar Pradesh: the Taj Mahal and Agra's Mughal monuments, Varanasi's ghats and the UNESCO-listed Buddhist site of Sarnath.

images.alt: Boats on the Ganga in front of Dashashwamedh Ghat in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
images.caption: Dashashwamedh Ghat, Varanasi

overview.text:
Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India and, by the Ministry of Tourism's count, the most visited: it recorded 646.81 million domestic tourist visits in 2024, more than a fifth of the national total, along with 2.27 million foreign tourist visits. Lucknow is the state capital, but most travellers come for two places in particular.

Agra holds three World Heritage Sites — the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri — and the Taj Mahal is the country's most visited ticketed monument for both Indian and foreign visitors. Further east, Varanasi sits on the Ganga, and just outside it the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026.

Use this page as a starting point: the destination guides below cover each city in detail, with visiting rules, getting there, where to stay and ready-made itineraries.

items.body: Agra and Varanasi are far apart — plan an overnight train or a flight between them rather than a day trip.
Check each monument's weekly closing day before you fix your dates — the destination guides list them.
In the hotter months, plan outdoor sightseeing for early morning and late afternoon.

places.name: Rajasthan
places.summary: India's largest state: the forts and palaces of Jaipur, Udaipur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer, the Thar Desert and tiger country at Ranthambore.
places.seoTitle: Rajasthan Travel Guide: Jaipur, Forts, Palaces & Desert
places.seoDescription: Plan a Rajasthan trip: Jaipur's forts and palaces, the UNESCO-listed hill forts, the Thar Desert, wildlife at Ranthambore and Keoladeo, and when to go.

images.commons: File:A bird eye view of Amer Fort Jaipur, India.jpg
images.alt: Aerial view of Amer Fort on its hillside above Maota Lake near Jaipur, Rajasthan
images.caption: Amer Fort above Maota Lake, Jaipur

overview.text:
Rajasthan is India's largest state by area, formed in 1949 from the merger of 22 kingdoms and principalities — which is why it has so many forts and palaces. It recorded 230 million domestic and 2.07 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, fifth among Indian states on both counts.

Its cities are known by colour: Jaipur the pink city, Jodhpur the blue, Udaipur the white and Jaisalmer the golden. Six of its hill forts, including Amber near Jaipur, are together a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Beyond the cities lie the Thar Desert, the bird sanctuary at Keoladeo — another World Heritage Site — and the tiger reserve at Ranthambore.

Most first trips start in Jaipur, the state capital and the third point of the Golden Triangle with Delhi and Agra. The guides below cover each destination in detail.

items.body: Distances are long — plan overnight trains or flights between far-apart cities like Jaipur and Jaisalmer.
In the hot months, plan forts and walking for early morning and late afternoon.
Many forts involve steep climbs and uneven paths — wear sturdy shoes.

places.name: Maharashtra
places.summary: India's leading state for foreign visitors: Mumbai's heritage and food, the rock-cut caves of Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta, the Konkan coast and the Western Ghats.
places.seoTitle: Maharashtra Travel Guide: Mumbai, Ajanta, Ellora & Konkan
places.seoDescription: Plan a Maharashtra trip: Mumbai's World Heritage architecture and Elephanta Caves, Ajanta and Ellora, the Konkan coast, Western Ghats treks and local food.

images.alt: The Gothic Revival facade and central dome of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai
images.caption: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai

overview.text:
Maharashtra received more foreign tourist visits than any other Indian state in 2024 — 3.70 million — largely because Mumbai, its capital, is one of India's main international gateways. It is the land where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in the 17th century, and its forts and temples still carry that history.

The state's World Heritage Sites span two thousand years: the rock-cut caves of Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta, and in Mumbai, the Gothic Revival Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensembles around the Oval Maidan. Beyond the cities, the state runs from the beaches of the Konkan coast up into the Sahyadri ranges of the Western Ghats.

Come hungry: vada pav, misal pav, puran poli and modak are all Maharashtrian classics, and Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated here with more fervour than anywhere else.

items.body: Avoid the coast and the Ghats at the height of the monsoon if you want easy travel — roads and ferries can be disrupted.
Book trains and hotels early around Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali.
Ajanta and Ellora are a long way from Mumbai — plan them as a separate leg of the trip rather than a day out.

places.name: Tamil Nadu
places.summary: Temple country of the south: Pallava and Chola monuments, Chennai, the Nilgiri hills and Tamil food, music and dance.
places.seoTitle: Tamil Nadu Travel Guide: Chennai, Temples & Mahabalipuram
places.seoDescription: Plan a Tamil Nadu trip: Chennai, the Pallava monuments of Mahabalipuram, the Great Living Chola Temples, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, food and festivals.

images.commons: File:Gopurams of Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Mylapore, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India (2012).jpg
images.alt: The carved gopurams of the Kapaleeshwarar Temple in Mylapore, Chennai
images.caption: Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Chennai

overview.text:
Tamil Nadu recorded 306.8 million domestic tourist visits in 2024 — the second most of any state — and 1.16 million foreign visits. It is above all a land of temples: its World Heritage Sites include the Pallava monuments of Mahabalipuram and the Great Living Chola Temples, alongside the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

Tamil culture is a draw in its own right — Carnatic music, Bharatanatyam dance, and meals served on a banana leaf with sambar and coconut chutney. Pongal, the harvest festival, is the year's great celebration.

Most visitors start in Chennai, the capital, and follow the coast south to Mahabalipuram and on to Puducherry.

items.body: Dress modestly and remove your shoes at temples; some inner sanctums are for Hindus only.
Temple towns get very busy at festival times — book rooms early.

places.name: Bihar
places.summary: The land of the Buddha: Bodh Gaya, Rajgir and Nalanda, the birthplace of Buddhism and Jainism, Madhubani art and the Chhath festival.
places.seoTitle: Bihar Travel Guide: Bodh Gaya, Nalanda & Rajgir
places.seoDescription: Plan a Bihar trip: Bodh Gaya's Mahabodhi Temple, the ruins of Nalanda, Rajgir's sacred hills, Madhubani art, Chhath and the best time to visit.

images.alt: The tall carved spire of the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya
images.caption: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya

overview.text:
Bihar takes its name from 'vihara', a Buddhist monastery, and it is the birthplace of both Buddhism and Jainism. The Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, taught on the hills of Rajgir, and Nalanda grew into one of the ancient world's great universities. Foreign tourist visits reached 0.737 million in 2024, up 35% on the year before.

Patna, the state capital, was once Pataliputra, and its Takhat Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, is revered by Sikhs. Bihar's living culture is just as distinctive: Madhubani painting, made by women of the Mithila region, and Chhath, the festival to the Sun God, usually between late October and mid-November.

items.body: The Buddhist sites are spread out — hire a car and driver to link them.
Book rooms early in winter, the main pilgrimage season.

places.name: West Bengal
places.summary: From Kolkata's culture and Durga Puja to the Sundarbans mangroves and the tea hills of Darjeeling.
places.seoTitle: West Bengal Travel Guide: Kolkata, Darjeeling & Sundarbans
places.seoDescription: Plan a West Bengal trip: Kolkata's museums and Durga Puja, the Sundarbans, Bishnupur's terracotta temples, Darjeeling's toy train and Bengali sweets.

images.alt: The white marble Victoria Memorial in Kolkata with its central dome and gardens
images.caption: Victoria Memorial, Kolkata

overview.text:
West Bengal runs from the Bay of Bengal to the Himalaya. Kolkata, its capital, is known as India's cultural capital and is home to the Indian Museum, founded in 1814, and the Victoria Memorial; Bishnupur has terracotta temples, and the Sundarbans mangrove forest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the north lie the tea gardens of Darjeeling.

The state's grandest festival is Durga Puja, celebrated over nine days with elaborate pandals, and Bengali food — from hilsa to rasogolla and sandesh — is a highlight of any trip. West Bengal received 3.12 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, second among Indian states.

items.body: Hilsa (ilish) and prawn dishes such as malai curry.
Rasogolla, sandesh and rasamalai — Bengal's famous milk sweets.
Visit Kolkata during Durga Puja for the pandals — and book early.

places.name: Punjab
places.summary: Land of the Golden Temple: Amritsar, Sikh heritage at Anandpur Sahib, Patiala's Qila Mubarak, the Harike wetland and famous Punjabi food.
places.seoTitle: Punjab Travel Guide: Amritsar, Golden Temple & More
places.seoDescription: Plan a Punjab trip: Amritsar's Golden Temple and Jallianwala Bagh, Virasat-e-Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib, Patiala's Qila Mubarak and the Harike wetland.

images.commons: File:Golden Temple or Harmandir Sahib - AMRITSAR.JPG
images.alt: The gilded Harmandir Sahib reflected in the Amrit Sarovar pool, Amritsar, under a cloudy sky
images.caption: The Golden Temple, Amritsar

overview.text:
Punjab is the heartland of Sikhism. In Amritsar, the Golden Temple is the faith's spiritual centre, where the langar serves free meals to all, and nearby Jallianwala Bagh recalls the massacre of 1919. At Anandpur Sahib, Virasat-e-Khalsa tells the story of the Sikh community, and the town hosts Hola Mohalla, a festival of martial arts and culture.

Beyond the Sikh sites, Patiala's Qila Mubarak and Kapurthala's mirrored Sheesh Mahal, inspired by Versailles, recall the state's royal past, and Harike Wetland, where the Beas and Sutlej meet, is the largest wetland in northern India. Punjab recorded 27.7 million domestic and 0.54 million foreign tourist visits in 2024.

items.body: Base yourself in Amritsar for the Golden Temple and the Wagah ceremony.
Carry a scarf for visits to gurdwaras.

places.name: Jammu and Kashmir
places.summary: Dal Lake and the Mughal gardens of Srinagar, Gulmarg's slopes, Pahalgam's valleys and the pilgrimages to Amarnath and Vaishno Devi — check advisories first.
places.seoTitle: Jammu and Kashmir Travel Guide & Current Advisories
places.seoDescription: Jammu and Kashmir: Srinagar's Dal Lake and Mughal gardens, Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Amarnath and Vaishno Devi, Kashmiri food — and the travel advisories to check first.

images.alt: Boatmen paddling across a still Dal Lake below snow-covered mountains
images.caption: Dal Lake, Srinagar

overview.text:
Jammu and Kashmir recorded 23.0 million domestic and 0.065 million foreign tourist visits in 2024. Its houseboats on the Dal and Nigeen lakes, spring tulips and mountain resorts draw visitors to the Kashmir Valley, while the Amarnath cave and the Vaishno Devi Temple draw pilgrims from across India. In Jammu, try khatta meat, madra and khameera bread.

Check current travel advice before planning a trip. As of October 2026, the UK government advises against all travel to the Union Territory, including Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg, except air travel to and within Jammu city. On 22 April 2025, militants killed 26 civilians, most of them tourists, near Pahalgam.

items.title: Travel advisories
items.body: As of October 2026, the UK government advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir, including Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg (air travel to and within Jammu city excepted). Check your own government's current advice and your insurance before planning a trip.

items.title: Recent violence
items.body: On 22 April 2025, militants killed 26 civilians, most of them tourists, near Pahalgam.
